name: Big Chuck

debut.episode: Let's Do the Time War Again

abilities: Eats solid matter (swallowed Eon's sword) with strong prehensile tongues
Spits ingested matter back out as explosive energy
weaknesses: No weaknesses documented on the wiki
Much smaller than Way Big (all Way Big fusions shrink unless the partner is equally huge)
summary: Ben 10,000's Biomnitrix fusion of Perk Upchuck and Way Big: a To'kustar-finned Upchuck who eats weapons whole and spits them back as explosions with a fraction of Way Big's might.
traits: Voice is OV Way Big's (Eric Bauza)
Way Big's chin eyes and head fin on an Upchuck body
notableFeats: Ate Eon's sword and took out Eon's minions with ease (Let's Do the Time War Again)

appearances.firstEpisode: Let's Do the Time War Again
notableEpisodes: Let's Do the Time War Again
appearances.designNotes: Perk Upchuck's basic body with Way Big's details: Way Big-style fins on head, elbows and shoulders in Perk Upchuck green, head bulbs turned fin-like, white face with grey top and green sides/back/neck, black arm stripes, tiny thighs with big calves, green fingers/toes, Way Big's chin eyes; Biomnitrix symbol on chest.

scoring.rationale: To'kustar-scale strength and speed in a compact body (wrecked Eon's minions effortlessly) combined with Upchuck's eat-anything-and-explode-it trick, giving strong offense and useful range. Only one outing, far smaller than Way Big and no cosmic ray shown.

notes: One-time form used only by the Omniverse Ben 10,000 via the Biomnitrix (Let's Do the Time War Again, OV S8).
Per Derrick J. Wyatt, Way Big combinations are smaller than Way Big unless fused with something equally large.

Biomnitrix context: the Omniverse Ben 10,000 (Original Future timeline, re-established as Ben Prime's true future) wears two linked Omnitrix gauntlets; slamming them together fuses two aliens on the fly (combinations are generated at transformation time, not stored). Each gauntlet alone gives normal aliens; it is voice-controlled and can be knocked out by a large EMP or Chronosapien time-freeze. All on-screen fusions were drawn by Thomas N. Perkins IV; the device name was coined by Derrick J. Wyatt (unnamed in scripts).
